note: Attacker-controlled glTF JSON bytes are passed to the ASCII loader; the JSON contains an image with an embedded base64 data URI.

code: bool ret = LoadASCIIFromString(model, err, warn, str, size, base_dir, 0);
note: The raw input string is forwarded into the JSON parser and image parsing path.
The image 'uri' field is a data URI; DecodeDataURI base64-decodes it into the byte vector 'img' (17 bytes: 54 01 09 d3 dd 00 00 10 61 7a cb f0 07 00 09 d1 10).

code: return (*LoadImageData)(image, image_idx, err, warn, 0, 0, &img.at(0), static_cast<int>(img.size()), load_image_user_data);
note: The decoded image bytes and their size are passed to the default LoadImageData callback.
The 17 decoded bytes are handed to stb_image's memory loader for format detection and decoding.
stbi__tga_test() recognizes the bytes as a TGA (offset=0x54, colormap type=1, image type=9 RLE colormapped), so the TGA decoder is invoked.
Header parse yields tga_palette_len=0, tga_palette_bits=16, tga_width=7, tga_height=53513, tga_bits_per_pixel=16; tga_indexed=1 so tga_comp=stbi__tga_get_comp(16,0,&tga_rgb16)=3 (RGB), tga_rgb16=1.
Palette buffer is allocated with size tga_palette_len*tga_comp = 0*3 = 0 bytes; malloc returns a 1-byte region, so the palette holds no valid entries.
In the indexed pixel loop, pal_idx is always >= tga_palette_len (0), so it is clamped to 0; the bounds check only compares against the entry count, not the byte size of the palette.

For j=0..2 the code reads tga_palette[0], tga_palette[1], tga_palette[2] from a 1-byte allocation, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ past the end of the palette buffer (ASAN: READ of size 1 at 0x6020000001d1, 0 bytes to the right of a 1-byte region).
